title: Induction Coil Overheat
shortDescription: One of the induction coils has exceeded its thermal limit.
fullDescription: Error E1 indicates the temperature sensor under an induction coil measured an unsafe temperature. The cooktop shuts down that zone until it cools. Empty pots, warped bases, or a clogged ventilation fan are common triggers.

causes.cause: Empty or dry pot on the burner

fixSteps.title: Remove the pot
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the cookware off the zone and allow it to cool.

fixSteps.title: Clear ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure nothing blocks the fan intake below the cooktop in the cabinet.

whenToCallPro: If E1 persists after cooldown with nothing on the zone, the coil sensor needs professional service.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop E1 coil overheat error fix

title: Unsuitable Cookware
shortDescription: The cooktop cannot detect ferromagnetic cookware.
fullDescription: Error E2 is displayed when a zone cannot detect a compatible pan. Induction requires ferromagnetic base metal; glass, aluminium, or copper without a ferro layer will not work.

causes.cause: Pan too small for the zone

fixSteps.title: Check the pan
fixSteps.instruction: Test with a magnet; it must stick firmly to the base.

fixSteps.title: Use correct size
fixSteps.instruction: Match pan diameter to the zone (minimum marked on the glass).

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed. If magnet sticks strongly and E2 persists, call service.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop E2 cookware error fix

faq.q: Do I need all new pots?
faq.a: Only if yours are not induction-ready. Check with a magnet first.

title: Electronics Overheat
shortDescription: The electronics compartment exceeded its safe operating temperature.
fullDescription: Error E3 indicates the inverter PCB temperature is too high. The cooktop throttles power or shuts down all zones until cooling is restored. Poor cabinet ventilation is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Clear ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Remove items from the cabinet below that block airflow.

fixSteps.title: Let cooktop cool
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and wait 20 minutes before reusing.

fixSteps.title: Check the fan
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for bearing noise and verify spin by hand with power off.

whenToCallPro: If the fan is dead and the cooktop is flush-installed, a pro can remove it safely.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop E3 overheat error fix

faq.q: Is a gap required under the cooktop?
faq.a: Yes. Follow the installation manual — typically at least 50 mm front-to-back airflow.

title: Mains Voltage Out Of Range
shortDescription: The input voltage is too high or too low.
fullDescription: Error E4 indicates the cooktop detected mains voltage outside its safe operating range. This can be a utility problem, a loose wire in the terminal block, or a miswired two-phase install.

causes.cause: Mains voltage too high or too low

fixSteps.title: Check utility
fixSteps.instruction: Verify other appliances and lights are normal. If flicker is widespread, call the utility.

fixSteps.title: Call an electrician
fixSteps.instruction: Have the terminal block and branch circuit inspected.

videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop E4 voltage error fix

faq.a: Yes. Low or high voltage can harm the inverter. Stop using until resolved.

title: General Control Fault
shortDescription: The cooktop has detected an unspecified internal error.
fullDescription: Error F0 is a generic fault raised when the inverter board detects an internal problem that does not match a more specific code. A power-cycle often clears transients; persistent F0 requires board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle the cooktop
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 10 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: If F0 returns, the inverter board needs professional diagnosis.

faq.a: No. Stop using the cooktop until the board is diagnosed.

title: Touch Control Fault
shortDescription: The touch control panel is unresponsive or reports a stuck key.
fullDescription: Error F1 indicates a stuck key or failed touch sensor on the glass surface. Water, debris, or a cracked glass touch area are common causes.

causes.cause: Liquid or crumbs on touch pad

symptoms: Keys do not respond or respond randomly

fixSteps.title: Clean the glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the touch area dry. Avoid metal objects on the surface.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the breaker off for 5 minutes and back on.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning and power-cycle do not work, the touch module needs replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop F1 touch error fix

faq.q: Can I use towels on the cooktop?
faq.a: Never during use — towels over the touch area cause false presses and F1.

title: Induction Coil Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A coil temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: Error F2 indicates the NTC sensor under one of the induction coils is providing invalid readings. The affected zone is disabled.

causes.cause: Sensor connector unseated on inverter board

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power
fixSteps.instruction: Cut the breaker and wait 10 minutes for capacitors to discharge.

fixSteps.title: Call a technician
fixSteps.instruction: Cooktop glass removal is required; best done by service.

whenToCallPro: Always — glass removal risks cracks if mishandled.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop F2 coil sensor error fix

faq.q: Can I use the other zones?
faq.a: Usually yes; only the faulty zone is disabled.

title: Glass Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The glass surface temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription: Error F3 indicates the sensor monitoring the glass temperature above the coil is open or shorted. This sensor protects the glass from cracking under extreme heat.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker before any service.

fixSteps.title: Call a technician
fixSteps.instruction: Replacement requires access to the coil assembly.

whenToCallPro: Always — safety sensor for glass protection.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop F3 glass sensor error fix

faq.q: Should I keep using the cooktop?
faq.a: Only with other zones; the affected zone will stay locked out.

title: Cooling Fan Failure
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan is not running.
fullDescription: Error F4 indicates the fan that cools the inverter has failed or is blocked. Without airflow the cooktop reduces power and eventually shuts down zones to avoid electronics overheat.

fixSteps.title: Clear the cabinet
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure no items block airflow under the cooktop.

videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop F4 fan error fix

faq.a: Yes. Flour and lint clog the intake over time.

title: Inverter Module Fault
shortDescription: One of the inverter power modules has failed.
fullDescription: Error F5 indicates an IGBT or inverter module has failed, often after a power surge or prolonged high-power use. The affected side of the cooktop is disabled.
symptoms: Multiple zones on one side dead

fixSteps.title: Cut power
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off the breaker and stop using the cooktop.

videoSearchQuery: Siemens cooktop F5 inverter error fix

faq.a: Often yes in the first two years — check your paperwork.
